parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the balancing of a metre ruler. Refer to Fig. 1.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Place the metre ruler on the pivot at the 50.0 cm mark. • Place the object Q with its centre on the metre ruler at the 90.0 cm mark. Determine the distance y from the 50.0 cm mark to the centre of the object Q. y = .................................................... cm [2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) • Place the 2.0 N load on the metre ruler. • Adjust the position of the load so that the metre ruler is as near as possible to being balanced.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Determine the distance x from the centre of the load to the 50.0 cm mark. x = .................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the weight W of object Q, using the equation W = x y × 2.0 N. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. W = ...................................................... N [2]

ms.label: 1(b)(ii)
ms.text:
Correct calculation of W
W given to 2 or 3 significant figures

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
New value for x less than previous value
W values equal within 10%

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
Statement to match results
Explanation with (W values quoted and) matching statement and results

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text:
A diagram clearly showing a suitable approach e.g. edges of object Q symmetrically either side of 90.0 cm mark.
Or wording describing the method.

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text:
Repeat and average OR Move the load back and forth / slowly (to establish the range within which the balance point resides
or until best balance).
